meta.subject: economics
meta.description: Economics facts: supply and demand, GDP, inflation, economic systems, money and banking, trade, taxes, entrepreneurship, personal finance, labor markets

facts.statement: Scarcity is the fundamental economic problem: unlimited wants but limited resources
Opportunity cost is the value of the next best alternative that is given up when making a choice
The three basic economic questions are: What to produce? How to produce? For whom to produce?
Goods are tangible products (books, cars); services are intangible activities performed for others (haircuts, teaching)
The four factors of production are land (natural resources), labor (workers), capital (tools/machinery), and entrepreneurship (innovation/risk-taking)
In a market economy, prices are determined by supply and demand with limited government intervention
In a command economy, the government makes most economic decisions about production and distribution
Most modern economies are mixed economies, combining elements of both market and command systems
A traditional economy is based on customs, traditions, and beliefs; economic decisions are made the way they have always been made
Incentives are rewards or penalties that motivate people to act in certain ways; they are a key concept in economics

common_errors.wrong: opportunity cost is always measured in money
common_errors.correct: Opportunity cost can be anything of value: time, enjoyment, other goods. If you choose to study instead of playing, the opportunity cost is the enjoyment of playing.

common_errors.wrong: scarcity only affects poor people
common_errors.correct: Scarcity affects everyone because even wealthy people have limited time and cannot have everything they want. It is a universal economic concept.

common_errors.wrong: the US has a pure market economy
common_errors.correct: The US has a mixed economy. While mostly market-based, the government regulates many industries, provides public services, and collects taxes.

common_errors.wrong: needs and wants are the same thing
common_errors.correct: Needs are essential for survival (food, shelter, clothing). Wants are things people desire but can live without (video games, designer clothes).

facts.statement: The law of demand states that as the price of a good increases, the quantity demanded decreases (and vice versa), all else being equal
The law of supply states that as the price of a good increases, the quantity supplied increases (and vice versa), all else being equal
Equilibrium price is the price at which the quantity supplied equals the quantity demanded in a market
A shortage occurs when demand exceeds supply at a given price; a surplus occurs when supply exceeds demand
Competition among sellers tends to lower prices and improve quality for consumers
A monopoly exists when one company controls an entire market, which can lead to higher prices and less innovation
Factors that shift demand include changes in income, tastes, prices of related goods, population, and expectations
Factors that shift supply include changes in input costs, technology, number of producers, and government regulations
Price controls like price ceilings (maximum prices) and price floors (minimum prices) can cause shortages or surpluses

common_errors.wrong: higher prices always mean companies are greedy
common_errors.correct: Prices are determined by supply and demand. Higher prices can result from increased costs, scarcity, or higher demand, not just seller decisions.

common_errors.wrong: supply and demand only apply to physical products
common_errors.correct: Supply and demand apply to services, labor, housing, currencies, and virtually all markets, not just physical goods.

common_errors.wrong: a shortage means there is no supply at all
common_errors.correct: A shortage means demand exceeds supply at the current price. There is still some supply, just not enough to meet all demand at that price.

common_errors.wrong: competition is bad for consumers
common_errors.correct: Competition among businesses generally benefits consumers by lowering prices, improving quality, and increasing choices.

facts.statement: A budget is a plan for how to spend and save money, tracking income and expenses
Simple interest is calculated as Principal x Rate x Time; compound interest earns interest on both the principal and previously accumulated interest
Credit is the ability to borrow money with the promise to repay it, usually with interest
A credit score is a numerical rating of a person's creditworthiness, based on their history of borrowing and repaying
The Rule of 72 estimates how long it takes money to double: divide 72 by the annual interest rate (e.g., 72/6 = 12 years at 6%)
Income tax is a percentage of earnings paid to the government; the US uses a progressive tax system where higher incomes are taxed at higher rates
Saving money means setting aside income for future use; investing means putting money into assets like stocks or bonds to earn a return over time
The FDIC (Federal Deposit Insurance Corporation) insures bank deposits up to $250,000 per depositor, per bank
A checking account is used for everyday spending; a savings account earns interest and is used to store money for the future

common_errors.wrong: saving money in a mattress is the same as saving in a bank
common_errors.correct: Money in a bank earns interest and is protected by FDIC insurance. Money at home earns nothing and can be lost to theft or disaster.

common_errors.wrong: all debt is bad
common_errors.correct: Some debt can be productive (student loans, mortgages) if it leads to increased future earnings or asset building. Excessive high-interest debt is harmful.

common_errors.wrong: compound interest only benefits savers
common_errors.correct: Compound interest works for savers (earning interest on interest) but also against borrowers (owing interest on interest).

common_errors.wrong: a credit card gives you free money
common_errors.correct: Credit card purchases must be repaid. Unpaid balances accrue interest, often at high rates (15-25%), making items cost much more over time.

facts.statement: Exports are goods and services sold to other countries; imports are goods and services bought from other countries
A tariff is a tax on imported goods that makes them more expensive, protecting domestic producers
Comparative advantage means a country can produce a good at a lower opportunity cost than another country, making trade beneficial for both
A trade deficit occurs when a country imports more than it exports; a trade surplus occurs when it exports more than it imports
Globalization is the increasing interconnection of economies, cultures, and populations worldwide through trade, technology, and communication
Free trade agreements (like USMCA, formerly NAFTA) reduce or eliminate tariffs and trade barriers between member countries
Exchange rates determine how much one country's currency is worth in terms of another country's currency
An embargo is a government ban on trade with a specific country, often used as a political tool or punishment

common_errors.wrong: trade only benefits the exporting country
common_errors.correct: Trade benefits both parties. The importing country gets goods it cannot produce as efficiently, and the exporting country earns revenue.

common_errors.wrong: tariffs only affect foreign companies
common_errors.correct: Tariffs raise prices for domestic consumers, since the cost of the tariff is typically passed on in higher retail prices.

common_errors.wrong: a trade deficit always means an economy is weak
common_errors.correct: A trade deficit can reflect strong consumer demand and investment inflows. The US has run trade deficits for decades during periods of economic growth.

common_errors.wrong: globalization only benefits wealthy countries
common_errors.correct: Globalization has both benefits and costs for all countries. Many developing nations have experienced economic growth through trade, though distribution of benefits varies.

facts.statement: Money serves three functions: medium of exchange (used to buy things), store of value (holds purchasing power), and unit of account (measures value)
The Federal Reserve (the Fed) is the central bank of the United States, responsible for monetary policy and regulating banks
Inflation is a general increase in prices over time, which reduces the purchasing power of money
GDP (Gross Domestic Product) is the total value of all goods and services produced in a country in a year, and is the most common measure of economic output
A recession is a significant decline in economic activity lasting at least several months, typically marked by falling GDP, rising unemployment, and declining business
The Federal Reserve can raise or lower interest rates to influence borrowing, spending, and inflation in the economy
Banks make money by charging higher interest rates on loans than they pay on deposits, a difference called the spread
Fiat money (like the US dollar) has value because the government declares it legal tender, not because it is backed by gold or silver
The Consumer Price Index (CPI) measures the average change in prices paid by consumers for a basket of goods and services over time

common_errors.wrong: the government prints money whenever it needs more
common_errors.correct: Printing too much money causes inflation. The Federal Reserve carefully controls the money supply to maintain price stability.

common_errors.wrong: inflation means everything costs more and everyone is worse off
common_errors.correct: Moderate inflation (around 2%) is considered normal and healthy. Wages often rise with inflation. Hyperinflation is the dangerous extreme.

common_errors.wrong: the US dollar is backed by gold
common_errors.correct: The US abandoned the gold standard in 1971. The dollar is now fiat money, backed by the full faith and credit of the US government.

common_errors.wrong: banks lend out all the money deposited in them
common_errors.correct: Banks are required to keep a reserve (a fraction of deposits) and lend out the rest. This is called fractional reserve banking.

facts.statement: The U.S. federal government is funded primarily through income taxes, payroll taxes, and corporate taxes
A progressive tax takes a larger percentage from higher-income earners; the federal income tax is progressive
A regressive tax takes a larger percentage from lower-income earners; sales taxes are considered regressive
The national debt is the total amount of money the federal government owes; it grows when the government spends more than it collects in taxes (deficit spending)
The largest categories of federal spending include Social Security, Medicare/Medicaid, and national defense
State and local governments rely heavily on sales taxes and property taxes for revenue
Fiscal policy refers to government decisions about taxing and spending to influence the economy
The 16th Amendment (1913) gave Congress the power to collect a federal income tax

common_errors.wrong: everyone pays the same tax rate
common_errors.correct: The US has a progressive income tax system where higher earners pay higher rates on income above certain thresholds.

common_errors.wrong: all taxes go to the federal government
common_errors.correct: Taxes are collected by federal, state, and local governments. Sales tax goes to the state, property tax to local government, and income tax to federal and sometimes state.

common_errors.wrong: the national debt and the deficit are the same thing
common_errors.correct: The deficit is the annual shortfall (spending minus revenue in one year). The national debt is the accumulated total of all past deficits.

facts.statement: An entrepreneur is someone who starts a business, taking on financial risk in the hope of making a profit
Profit is the money a business earns after subtracting all costs; loss occurs when costs exceed revenue
Small businesses account for nearly half of all private-sector employment in the United States
The stock market allows people to buy and sell shares (ownership stakes) in publicly traded companies
A corporation is a type of business that is legally separate from its owners, providing limited liability protection
Innovation and new technology drive economic growth by creating new products, services, and more efficient ways of producing things
A business plan is a written document that describes a business's goals, strategies, market analysis, and financial projections
The three main types of business ownership are sole proprietorship (one owner), partnership (two or more owners), and corporation (shareholders)

common_errors.wrong: all businesses make money right away
common_errors.correct: Most new businesses lose money in their first few years. Many startups fail within five years. Success usually requires sustained effort and adaptation.

common_errors.wrong: the stock market always goes up
common_errors.correct: The stock market fluctuates and can lose value in the short term. While it has generally trended upward over long periods, there are no guarantees.

common_errors.wrong: entrepreneurs don't take any risks
common_errors.correct: Entrepreneurship involves significant financial risk. Entrepreneurs invest their own money and time with no guarantee of success.

common_errors.wrong: profit and revenue are the same thing
common_errors.correct: Revenue is total money earned from sales. Profit is revenue minus all costs (materials, labor, rent, taxes). A business can have high revenue but low or negative profit.

facts.statement: The unemployment rate measures the percentage of the labor force that is actively looking for work but cannot find it
The minimum wage is the lowest hourly pay that employers are legally required to pay workers; the federal minimum wage can be different from state minimums
Human capital refers to the skills, education, and experience that make workers more productive and valuable
Labor unions are organizations of workers that negotiate collectively with employers for better wages, benefits, and working conditions
The labor force includes all people who are employed or actively seeking employment; it does not include retirees, students, or stay-at-home parents
Wages are determined by the supply of and demand for labor; workers with rare, in-demand skills tend to earn higher wages
Education and job training increase human capital, which generally leads to higher earning potential over a lifetime
The Fair Labor Standards Act (1938) established the minimum wage, overtime pay, and restrictions on child labor in the United States

common_errors.wrong: the unemployment rate counts everyone without a job
common_errors.correct: The unemployment rate only counts people who are actively seeking work. Retirees, students, and people who have stopped looking are not counted.

common_errors.wrong: raising the minimum wage has no effects beyond higher pay
common_errors.correct: Minimum wage increases can raise income for low-wage workers but may also lead some employers to reduce hours or hiring, depending on the amount of the increase.

common_errors.wrong: a college degree guarantees a high-paying job
common_errors.correct: While college graduates generally earn more on average, outcomes depend on the field of study, job market conditions, and individual skills.

facts.statement: The business cycle consists of four phases: expansion (growth), peak (highest point), contraction (decline), and trough (lowest point)
A depression is a severe and prolonged recession; the Great Depression (1929-1939) saw unemployment reach about 25% in the United States
Leading economic indicators help predict future economic activity; examples include stock market performance, building permits, and consumer confidence
Standard of living refers to the level of material comfort measured by goods, services, and luxuries available to a person or community
Per capita GDP divides a country's total GDP by its population, providing a rough measure of average economic output per person
Economic growth occurs when a country produces more goods and services over time, usually measured by increases in real GDP
The Great Recession of 2007-2009 was triggered by the collapse of the US housing market and led to a global financial crisis
Productivity measures the amount of output produced per unit of input; higher productivity leads to economic growth and potentially higher wages

common_errors.wrong: a recession means the economy has completely stopped
common_errors.correct: A recession is a significant decline in activity, but the economy still functions. People still work, buy goods, and businesses still operate -- just at reduced levels.

common_errors.wrong: GDP measures how happy people are
common_errors.correct: GDP measures economic output, not well-being. A country can have high GDP but still have inequality, pollution, or low quality of life.

common_errors.wrong: recessions can be completely prevented
common_errors.correct: While government policies can moderate economic cycles, recessions are a natural part of the business cycle. Preventing all downturns is not realistic.

common_errors.wrong: economic growth always benefits everyone equally
common_errors.correct: Economic growth can increase overall wealth while still leaving some groups behind. The distribution of benefits depends on policies, institutions, and market conditions.

facts.statement: Consumers are people who buy and use goods and services; producers are people or businesses that make and sell goods and services
Consumers make choices based on price, quality, brand, needs, and preferences; these choices drive what producers make
Advertising tries to influence consumer choices by creating awareness of products and persuading people to buy them
Consumer protection laws prevent businesses from selling unsafe products, using misleading advertising, or engaging in unfair practices
The circular flow model shows how money, goods, and services flow between households (consumers) and businesses (producers) in an economy
Consumer spending accounts for roughly two-thirds of total US economic activity, making it the largest component of GDP
Specialization means focusing on producing a limited range of goods or services, which increases efficiency and allows for trade
Natural resources, human resources, and capital resources are the three types of productive resources used to make goods and services

common_errors.wrong: advertising always tells the truth about products
common_errors.correct: While laws prohibit false advertising, ads are designed to persuade and may emphasize benefits while downplaying drawbacks. Consumers should evaluate claims critically.

common_errors.wrong: the most expensive product is always the best
common_errors.correct: Price does not always reflect quality. Higher prices can result from branding, marketing, or inefficiency rather than superior quality.

common_errors.wrong: consumers have no power in the economy
common_errors.correct: Consumer choices collectively determine what products succeed or fail. When consumers stop buying a product, businesses must adapt or close.
